thread:
maria: Hey — seeing a weird mismatch on the latency panel. p95 for /v1/generate shows ~180ms in the main view but when I click into endpoint breakdown for eu-west it lists p95 ~230ms. Tried a refresh, same. Anyone seen this?

ajay: Huh. Is that the new aggregation rollup mode (merge-mode=tdigest) we flipped last week? Could be a merge artifact.

maria: Yep, that's the one. I also noticed the sample counts differ: main panel shows ~12k samples, endpoint slice shows ~900 samples.

denise: If sample counts differ that much the t-digest rollup can produce non-intuitive quantiles when you merge summaries from very different bucket sizes. We hit this in a canary a while back.

moliver: Do we have a quick repro query? Can you dump the raw samples for that time window?

maria: Quick dump (filtered):
```
select route, sample_count, p50, p95, p99 from latency_rollups where route='/v1/generate' and region='eu-west' and ts between 1709098800 and 1709099100;
-- results: main_agg 12000 70 180 430
-- endpoint_slice 900 65 230 610
```

ajay: That looks like the classic small-slice bias. Also check routing policy — if quota fallback kicked in some requests might have gone to a slower variant, inflating p95 on the endpoint view.

denise: Good call. I checked routing logs: around 1709098920 we briefly hit a reserved-capacity throttle and a subset of requests fell back to the slower cpu-variant. That bump is concentrated in one caller bucket, which explains the endpoint-level spike but gets washed out in the global rollup.

maria: So product expects the panel to reflect what users see per-endpoint, but the main p95 is aggregated across many slices and that hides the spike. Need a clear UX so folks don't assume data is consistent across views.

moliver: Two quick fixes: 1) surface sample_count next to each percentile in the panel, 2) annotate the chart when we detect heavy skew (e.g., one slice >50% of tail contribution).

ajay: Also we should include a tooltip explaining "p95 is derived from t-digest merges — low-count slices may produce nonmonotonic or surprising values". Link to doc + small explainer. I can draft the tooltip.

denise: From infra side: permanent fix is to fall back to raw samples for any slice with sample_count < threshold (say 2000) when computing panel comparatives. That avoids the t-digest merge caveat in low-sample regimes. But that's more infra-work.

maria: Prioritization ask: can we do the UI badge + tooltip this week and file an infra ticket for the raw-sample fallback?

moliver: Yep. I'll open a tiny UX PR to add a "samples" badge and the tooltip. Assigning to @ajay for copy and @denise for infra ticket.

ajay: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/834 (WIP) — adds sample_count and tooltip.

denise: Filing infra ticket now: INFRA-4281 — "fallback to raw-samples for low-count slice quantile compare". I'll add suggested threshold and unit tests.

maria: Thanks. Also can we add a one-line dashboard annotation indicating quota fallback window? That would have made this easier to spot.

moliver: Good idea. I'll add an annotation when routing policy emits a fallback event. That will show up as vertical band on latency charts.

console-bot: Deploy notice: Canary rollout 12 -> 25% for console PR #834 scheduled in 15m.

maria: Awesome — let's monitor the panel after the patch lands and then close out with a short runbook entry describing the t-digest caveat and steps to inspect sample-origin.

ajay: I'll update runbook and add a checklist: check sample_count, check routing fallback events, inspect per-caller slices.

denise: Adding unit tests for the raw-sample path and an alert if sample_count drops below threshold for any endpoint being used in SLO charts.

maria: Cool. Thanks all :thumbsup: 

Action items:
- ajay: finish tooltip copy + review UX PR (console#834)
- moliver: land UI badge + chart annotation
- denise: INFRA-4281 + unit tests + alerting
- maria: update runbook and confirm post-deploy monitoring

Follow-up: check again at 1709099300 and confirm numbers converge or document the discrepancy.
